title: Proactive degradation simulation runbook for SLO preservation across region loss and GPU pressure
creator: Samir Patel
description:
Objective: Run a controlled, repeatable simulation that validates how Redwood preserves customer-facing SLOs when a primary region becomes unavailable and/or GPU pools experience sudden exhaustion. The simulation focuses on three coordinated controls: routing failover, circuit-breaker hysteresis tuning, and intelligent load-shedding based on request scoring. We will verify that automated fallbacks and shed policies keep latency P95 and error-rate SLOs within tolerances while minimizing costly overprovisioning.

Scope: - Primary region evacuation (control-plane and data-plane routing cut) - GPU pool rapid exhaustion (simulate N GPUs failing or preempted) - Upstream dependency silence/slowdown (embedding store and feature-store queries) - Exercise dynamic circuit-breaker thresholds, cooldown windows, and adaptive rejection to protect critical paths.

Out-of-scope: Simulating hardware faults beyond GPU eviction behavior, long-term capacity planning, or customer data-loss scenarios. This is a resilience/regression test of serving and routing behaviors, not a data-plane disaster recovery drill.
acceptance_criteria: Controlled run produces telemetry that demonstrates P95 latency < target and error rate within SLO for at least 95% of critical endpoints after automated failover and shedding is applied
Circuit-breaker thresholds automatically trip and recover without manual intervention; hysteresis parameters prevent oscillations in at least 90% of flows

Load-shedding policy correctly prioritizes critical routes (auth, health-checks, system-prompts) and rejects best-effort requests with documented metrics showing reduced token cost and preserved throughput for critical requests
Post-run analysis identifies actionable tuning adjustments and produces a prioritized set of follow-ups with performance regression risk assessment
Runbook and tooling are executable by on-call and SRE with <30 minutes setup time and documented rollback steps
runbook_steps: Pre-run: Notify stakeholders (SRE, Platform, PM, Solutions) and register maintenance window; snapshot current routing/config and baseline SLO metrics
Stage 1: Induce dependency slowdown by injecting 200-800ms latency to embedding-store endpoints via fault-proxy; observe slow-path behavior and circuit-breaker tripping for dependent handlers

Stage 2: Simulate GPU pool pressure by sequentially draining and preempting GPUs in the primary pool, ramping at 10% every 60s until 50% capacity reduction is reached; measure admission-control and shedding actions
Stage 3: Cut primary region egress to force smart-routing to use secondary regions and model variants with lower latency/cost; verify routing policy fallbacks and quota enforcement

Stage 4: Enable adaptive request-scoring shedder which uses model cost, user tier, and route criticality to decide rejections; validate that critical tokens are permitted and best-effort requests are rejected
Stage 5: Observe circuit-breaker cooldown and recovery behavior; intentionally create a brief recovery flapping to validate hysteresis safeguards and backoff windows
Post-run: Revert all injected faults, restore original routing and capacity, and run recovery validation tests; collect all telemetry and artifacts
metrics_to_collect: token throughput and GPU utilization per pool
admission control rejects and shed counts (by policy and route)
request scoring distribution and rejected-request trace samples
cross-region failover latency and time-to-first-success metrics
observability_queries: logs/query: service:serving AND level:ERROR AND tag:failover
